Given:
Distribution of students and their marks:

10 students scored 20 marks

6 students scored 19 marks

5 students scored 18 marks

4 students scored 17 marks

2 students scored 12 marks

Formula Used:
Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total students = 10 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 27
⇒ Total marks = (10 × 20) + (6 × 19) + (5 × 18) + (4 × 17) + (2 × 12)
⇒ Total marks = 200 + 114 + 90 + 68 + 24
⇒ Total marks = 496
⇒ Average marks = 496 ÷ 27
⇒ Average marks ≈ 18.3703...
∴ The correct answer is 18.37 marks.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When data sets have different frequencies or weights, the weighted average is calculated as Sum(wi × xi) ÷ Sum(wi), where w is the respective frequency and x is the value.

Assumed Mean Deviation Method

A faster way to find averages involves picking an assumed mean (A), calculating total deviation (D) of all items from A, and finding True Average = A + (D ÷ N).

Combined Average

For two groups with sizes n1 and n2 and averages A1 and A2, the combined average is given by the formula (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

questions.question: A candidate who scores 20% of the marks falls short by 10 marks to pass the exam, while another candidate who scores 42% of the marks surpasses the passing marks by 12%. What is the maximum number of marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Difference in percentage = 42% − 20% = 22%

In terms of marks, 42% is 12% of total marks above passing and 20% is 10 marks below passing.

Let maximum marks be M. Passing marks = 0.20M + 10. Also, 0.42M = (Passing marks) + 0.12M.

⇒ 0.42M − 0.12M = 0.20M + 10 ⇒ 0.30M = 0.20M + 10 ⇒ 0.10M = 10.
∴ The correct answer is 100 marks.

Alternate Method
Let maximum marks be x.
Candidate 1: Score = 20% of x = 0.20x
Passing Marks = Score + Deficit = 0.20x + 10 --- (Equation 1)
Candidate 2: Score = 42% of x = 0.42x

This score is 12% of maximum marks more than passing marks.

⇒ Passing Marks = 0.42x − 12% of x = 0.42x − 0.12x = 0.30x --- (Equation 2)

Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 0.20x + 10 = 0.30x
⇒ 0.30x − 0.20x = 10
⇒ 0.10x = 10
⇒ x = 10 / 0.10 = 100
∴ The correct answer is 100 marks.

Additional Information
Passing Percentage
It is the minimum percentage required to pass. Passing % = (Passing Marks / Maximum Marks) × 100.

Percentage Change
When comparing two scores, the difference in percentage points relates directly to the difference in actual marks via the base of Maximum Marks.

questions.question: A sector of a circle has a radius of 18 cm and a central angle of 125°. What will be its approximate perimeter? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Given:
Radius = 18 cm
Central angle = 125°

Formula used:
Perimeter of sector of a circle = (θ / 360°) × 2πr + 2r

Calculation:
According to the question:
Perimeter of sector of a circle = (125 / 360) × 2 × (22 / 7) × 18 + 2 × 18
⇒ (25 / 72) × (44 / 7) × 18 + 36
⇒ (275 / 7) + 36
⇒ (275 + 252) / 7
⇒ 527 / 7
⇒ 75.28 cm ~ 75.3 cm
∴ The required perimeter is 75.3 cm.

questions.question: 36 workmen are employed to finish a certain work in 48 days. But it is found that in 24 days, only 2/5 work is done. How many more men must be taken to finish the work in time?
questions.solution:
Given:
36 workmen can do 2/5 part of a work in 24 days.

Concept:
Total work = (Number of men × Time taken) / part of work done

Calculation:
Total work = (36 × 24) / (2/5) units = 2160 units
Time required to complete the rest work = (48 - 24) days = 24 days
Let extra workers required to complete the work in time be x, then:
{(x + 36) × 24} / (1 - 2/5) = 2160 units
⇒ {(x + 36) × 24} / (3/5) = 2160 units
⇒ x + 36 = (2160 / 24) × (3 / 5)
⇒ x + 36 = 90 × 3 / 5
⇒ x = 54 - 36 = 18 workers
∴ 18 extra workers are required to do the same work in 48 days.

questions.question: The average of 5 results is 46 and that of the first four is 45. The fifth result is:
questions.solution: Since the average of 5 results is 46, the sum of 5 values is 5 × 46 = 230. Sum of first 4 values is 4 × 45 = 180. Hence the fifth number is 230 - 180 = 50.

questions.question: A dealer sells an article by allowing a 20% discount on its marked price and still gains 12%. If the cost price of the article is Rs. 750, then its marked price (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution: Use the direct relation: CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%). CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 12) = 80 : 112 = 5 : 7. Given Cost Price (CP) = 5 units = ₹750, so 1 unit = 750 ÷ 5 = 150. Marked Price (MP) = 7 units = 7 × 150 = 1050.

questions.question: The distance between two stations A and B is 700 km. A train covers the journey from A to B at a speed of 80 km/h and returns back to A with a uniform speed of 65 km/h. The average speed of train during the whole journey, is closest to:
questions.solution:
Given:
Distance between A and B = 700 km
Speed of train from A to B = 80 km/h
Speed of train from B to A = 65 km/h

Concept used:
Distance = Speed × Time
Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time taken

Calculation:
Time taken by train from A to B = Distance / Speed = 700 / 80
Time taken by train from B to A = 700 / 65
Average speed during the whole journey = Total distance / Total time
⇒ (700 + 700) / [(700 / 80 + 700 / 65)]
⇒ (700 + 700) / [700 × (1 / 80 + 1 / 65)]
⇒ (2 × 700) / [700 × (13 + 16) / 1040]
⇒ 2 / (29 / 1040)
⇒ (1040 × 2) / 29 = 71.72 km/h
∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.

Shortcut Trick:
If the distance travelled in both the cases is the same, then we can apply this formula:
Average speed = (2 × product of the two speeds) / (Sum of the two speeds)
⇒ (2 × 80 × 65) / (80 + 65)
⇒ 10400 / 145 = 71.72 km/h
∴ The average speed of the train during the whole journey is 71.72 km/h.

questions.question: A person invested a total of Rs. 57,500 at 4%, 5% and 8% per annum simple interest. At the end of the year, he received equal interest in all the three cases. The amount invested at 5% was:
questions.solution:
Given:
Principal = 57,500
Rate of interest = 4%, 5% and 8%

Formula used:
S.I = (P × R × T) / 100

Calculation:
Let the three parts be x, y and z
Then,
⇒ (x × 4 × 1) / 100 = (y × 5 × 1) / 100 = (z × 8 × 1) / 100
⇒ 0.04x = 0.05y = 0.08z
⇒ x : y : z = 10 : 8 : 5
Sum invested at 5% = (8 / 23) × 57,500 = 20,000
∴ The answer is Rs 20,000.

questions.question: The LCM and HCF of two positive numbers are 96 and 8, respectively. If the sum of the numbers is 56, then the difference between the numbers is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick:
Let the numbers be 8x and 8y, where x and y are co-prime.
Product of ratios (x × y) = LCM ÷ HCF = 96 ÷ 8 = 12.
Sum of ratios (x + y) = Sum ÷ HCF = 56 ÷ 8 = 7.
Find two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7 → 3 and 4.
Difference between numbers = HCF × (x − y) = 8 × (4 − 3) = 8.
∴ The correct answer is 8.

Alternate Method:
Given:
LCM = 96, HCF = 8, Sum (a + b) = 56.

Formula Used:
Product of two numbers (a × b) = LCM × HCF
Algebraic identity: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

Calculations:
⇒ Product (ab) = 96 × 8 = 768
⇒ Sum (a + b) = 56
⇒ (a − b)² = (56)² − 4 × (768)
⇒ (a − b)² = 3136 − 3072
⇒ (a − b)² = 64
⇒ (a − b) = √64 = 8
∴ The correct answer is 8.

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 495 and their HCF is 5. If the sum of the numbers is 100, then their difference is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick:
Let the two numbers be 5a and 5b, where a and b are coprime.
Given LCM = 495 ⇒ 5 × a × b = 495 ⇒ a × b = 99
Given Sum = 100 ⇒ 5a + 5b = 100 ⇒ a + b = 20
Values satisfying both conditions are a = 11 and b = 9.
Difference = 5a − 5b = 5 × (11 − 9) = 10.
∴ The correct answer is 10.

Alternate Method:
Given:
LCM of the two numbers = 495
HCF of the two numbers = 5
Sum of the numbers (a + b) = 100

Formula Used:
Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM
(a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

Calculations:
⇒ a × b = 5 × 495 = 2475
⇒ (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab
⇒ (a − b)² = (100)² − 4 × 2475
⇒ (a − b)² = 10000 − 9900
⇒ (a − b)² = 100
⇒ a − b = √100
⇒ a − b = 10
∴ The correct answer is 10.

questions.question: For what relation between a and b is the equation sin θ = (a + b) / (2√(ab)) possible?
questions.solution:
Given:
Sin θ = (a + b) / (2√(ab))

Concept:
-1 ≤ sin θ ≤ +1

Calculation:
-1 ≤ (a + b) / (2√(ab)) ≤ +1
We solve one of them:
(a + b) / (2√(ab)) ≤ 1
⇒ a + b ≤ 2√(ab)
⇒ a + b - 2√(ab) ≤ 0
⇒ (√a - √b)² ≤ 0
⇒ √a = √b ⇒ a = b
∴ The correct answer is a = b

Shortcut Trick:
We can solve this question by options to satisfy the equation.
Put a = b
Then Sin θ = (a + a) / (2√(a × a))
Sin θ = 2a / 2a = 1 (since sin θ ≤ 1)

questions.question: The income of A is 40% more than the income of B, and the income of C is 30% less than the total incomes of A and B. The income of A is what per cent less than the income of C?
questions.solution: Shortcut Trick: Let Income of B = 100. Income of A = 140 (40% more than B). Income of C = 70% of (140 + 100) = 0.7 × 240 = 168. Difference between C and A = 168 − 140 = 28. Required % = (28 ÷ 168) × 100 = 1/6 × 100 = 16(2/3)%. ∴ The correct answer is 16(2/3)%.

questions.question: If the 11-digit number 79x6402087y is divisible by 72, then for smallest value of x, what is the value of (x + 2y)?
questions.solution: For a number to be divisible by 72, it must be perfectly divisible by both 8 and 9. Rule of 8: The last three digits (87y) must be divisible by 8 ⇒ 872 is divisible by 8, so y = 2. Rule of 9: The sum of digits (45 + x) must be divisible by 9 ⇒ The smallest possible value for x is 0. Required value = (x + 2y) = 0 + 2 × 2 = 4. ∴ The correct answer is 4.

questions.question: To pack a set of books, Gautam got cartons of a certain height that were 48 inches long and 27 inches wide. If the volume of such a carton was 22.5 cubic feet, what was the height of each carton? [Use 1 foot = 12 inches.]
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Convert the given volume directly into cubic inches by multiplying by 12^3.

Volume in inches = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch^3
Since Volume = Length × Width × Height
Height = 38880 ÷ (48 × 27)
Height = 38880 ÷ 1296 = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Alternate Method
Given:
Length (L) = 48 inches
Width (B) = 27 inches
Volume (V) = 22.5 ft^3
1 ft = 12 inches

Formula Used:
Volume of a cuboid = L × B × H

Calculations:
⇒ Volume in inch^3 = 22.5 × 12 × 12 × 12
⇒ Volume = 22.5 × 1728 = 38880 inch^3
⇒ L × B × H = 38880
⇒ 48 × 27 × H = 38880
⇒ 1296 × H = 38880
⇒ H = 38880 ÷ 1296
⇒ H = 30 inches
∴ The correct answer is 30 inches.

Additional Information
Volume of a Cuboid
V = L × B × H, where L, B, and H denote length, breadth, and height respectively.
Surface Area of a Cuboid
Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2(LB + BH + HL). Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 2H(L + B).
Diagonal of a Cuboid
The length of the longest space diagonal inside a cuboid is √(L^2 + B^2 + H^2).
Unit Conversions
Since 1 foot = 12 inches, calculating volume requires taking the cube of 12. Thus, 1 cubic foot = 12^3 = 1728 cubic inches.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of diameter 16 cm is full of ice cream. Each student in a class is served exactly 6 scoops of ice cream. If the hemispherical scoop is having a radius of 2 cm, then ice cream is served to approximately how many students?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Total number of scoops in the bowl = (Radius of bowl ÷ Radius of scoop)^3
⇒ Total scoops = (8 ÷ 2)^3 = 4^3 = 64 scoops
Since each student is served exactly 6 scoops:
⇒ Number of students served = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66

Ice cream can be fully served to a maximum of 10 students with exactly 6 scoops each.

∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Alternate Method
Given:
Diameter of the hemispherical bowl = 16 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm
Radius of the hemispherical scoop (r) = 2 cm
Scoops served per student = 6

Formula Used:
Volume of a hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3) × π × radius^3

Calculations:
⇒ Volume of the ice cream in the bowl = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 8^3 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 512
⇒ Volume of a single scoop = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 2^3 = (2 ÷ 3) × π × 8
⇒ Total number of scoops = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of single scoop
⇒ Total number of scoops = [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 512] ÷ [(2 ÷ 3) × π × 8] = 512 ÷ 8 = 64 scoops
⇒ Since each student receives exactly 6 scoops, the number of students = 64 ÷ 6 = 10.66
⇒ Thus, ice cream is fully served to 10 students, leaving exactly 4 scoops remaining in the bowl.
∴ The correct answer is 10 students.

Additional Information
Volume of a Hemisphere
A hemisphere is exactly half of a complete sphere. Its volume formula is V = (2 ÷ 3) × π × r^3.
Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Hemisphere
The TSA encompasses the curved surface along with the flat circular base. The formula is TSA = 3 × π × r^2.
Volume Proportionality Rule
For any pair of 3D shapes featuring identical proportions (like two spheres or hemispheres), the ratio of their total volumes equals the cube of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

questions.question: In a bag, the number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins but 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins. If the total amount in the bag is ₹270, what is the number of ₹5 coins?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y. Then ₹5 coins (20% less) = 4y, and ₹10 coins = 4y − 8.

Total value = 2(5y) + 5(4y) + 10(4y − 8) = 270.
10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270 ⇒ 70y = 350 ⇒ y = 5.
Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20.
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Alternate Method
Given:
Number of ₹5 coins is 8 more than the number of ₹10 coins.
Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less than the number of ₹2 coins.
Total amount in the bag = ₹270.

Formula Used:
Total Value = (Value of ₹2 coins) + (Value of ₹5 coins) + (Value of ₹10 coins)

Calculation:
⇒ Let the number of ₹2 coins be 5y.
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins is 20% less = 5y × (80 ÷ 100) = 4y
⇒ Number of ₹10 coins is 8 less than ₹5 coins = 4y − 8
⇒ Total value = (2 × 5y) + (5 × 4y) + 10 × (4y − 8) = 270
⇒ 10y + 20y + 40y − 80 = 270
⇒ 70y = 350
⇒ y = 350 ÷ 70 = 5
⇒ Number of ₹5 coins = 4 × 5 = 20
∴ The correct answer is 20.

Additional Information
Coins and Denominations
The total value of any denomination is calculated by multiplying the face value of the coin with the number of coins (Value = Denomination × Count).
Percentage Relationships
If quantity A is R% less than quantity B, then A = B × (100 − R) ÷ 100. This relationship is often used to find the ratio between multiple quantities quickly.
Linear Equations
Word problems often translate into linear equations format ax + b = c, where solving for the common ratio variable 'y' or 'x' gives the exact values for each parameter.

questions.question: The base of a triangular field is three times its altitude. If the cost of cultivating the field at Rs. 24.4/hect is Rs. 448.35, find its height. (in metres)
questions.solution:
Total Area = Total Cost ÷ Rate per hectare
Area = 448.35 ÷ 24.4 = 18.375 hectares = 183750 m²
Area of a triangle = ½ × Base × Height
½ × 3h × h = 183750 ⇒ h² = 122500
h = √122500 = 350 m
∴ The correct answer is 350 m.

questions.question: The average of 15 numbers is 80. The average of the first 6 numbers is 72. The average of the next 6 numbers is 25% more than the average of the first 6 numbers. The 13th number is 8 more than the 15th number, and the 14th number is 10 less than the 15th number. What is the average of the 13th and 14th numbers?
questions.solution:
Net deviation of first 12 numbers = 6 × (72 − 80) + 6 × (90 − 80) = −48 + 60 = +12
Sum of the 13th, 14th, and 15th numbers = (3 × 80) − 12 = 228
Assuming the 15th number is x: (x + 8) + (x − 10) + x = 228 ⇒ 3x = 230
Average of 13th and 14th numbers = [(x + 8) + (x − 10)] ÷ 2 = x − 1
Required Average = 230/3 − 1 = 227/3 ≈ 75.67
∴ The correct answer is 75.67.

questions.question: A toy manufacturer produced 1200 toy cars at a total cost of ₹90,000. He donated 200 cars to a charity event. For the rest, he announced a 10% discount on the market price of ₹120 per car. He also offered 2 toy cars free for every 8 toy cars purchased. If all 1200 toy cars were distributed, what is his overall gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Remaining cars after charity = 1200 − 200 = 1000.
Effective paid cars = 1000 × [8 ÷ (8 + 2)] = 800.
Selling Price (SP) per car = ₹120 − 10% = ₹108.
Total Revenue (SP) = 800 × ₹108 = ₹86,400.
Loss % = [(90,000 − 86,400) ÷ 90,000] × 100 = 4%.
∴ The correct answer is 4% loss.

questions.question: The number of red, blue, and green marbles in a bag is in the ratio 3 : 4 : 6. If 20 red marbles, 15 blue marbles, and an unknown number of green marbles are added to the bag, the ratio of red, blue, and green marbles becomes 4 : 5 : 7. Determine the number of green marbles added.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
By applying the cross-multiplication method on Red and Blue marbles:

Initial Ratio → 3 : 4 | Final Ratio → 4 : 5 | Quantity Added → +20, +15
1 initial ratio unit = [(4 × 15) − (5 × 20)] ÷ [(3 × 5) − (4 × 4)] = (60 − 100) ÷ (15 − 16) = 40.
Initial Green marbles = 6 × 40 = 240.
New Red marbles = (3 × 40) + 20 = 140, which represents 4 parts in the final ratio ⇒ 1 final unit = 140 ÷ 4 = 35.
New Green marbles = 7 × 35 = 245 ⇒ Green marbles added = 245 − 240 = 5.
∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial ratio of red, blue, and green marbles = 3 : 4 : 6
Marbles added = 20 red, 15 blue, and an unknown number of green marbles (y).
Final ratio of red, blue, and green marbles = 4 : 5 : 7
Initial Ratio
Red = 3x
Blue = 4x
Green = 6x
Final Ratio
Red = 4 parts
Blue = 5 parts
Green = 7 parts
+20
+15
+y

Calculations:
⇒ Let the initial number of red, blue, and green marbles be 3x, 4x, and 6x respectively.
⇒ After adding 20 red and 15 blue marbles, the new counts become (3x + 20) and (4x + 15).
⇒ Given the new ratio of red to blue is 4 : 5.
⇒ (3x + 20) ÷ (4x + 15) = 4 ÷ 5
⇒ 5 × (3x + 20) = 4 × (4x + 15)
⇒ 15x + 100 = 16x + 60
⇒ 16x − 15x = 100 − 60
⇒ x = 40
⇒ Initial red marbles = 3 × 40 = 120
⇒ Initial green marbles = 6 × 40 = 240
⇒ New red marbles = 120 + 20 = 140
⇒ Let the number of green marbles added be y. The new count of green marbles is (240 + y).
⇒ Given the new ratio of red to green is 4 : 7.
⇒ 140 ÷ (240 + y) = 4 ÷ 7
⇒ 240 + y = (140 × 7) ÷ 4
⇒ 240 + y = 35 × 7 = 245
⇒ y = 245 − 240 = 5
∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information
Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities, indicating how many times one number contains another. For quantities a and b, it is represented as a : b or the fraction a/b.

Cross-Multiplication Method in Ratios

When a given ratio a : b changes to c : d by adding quantities x and y respectively, the value of 1 initial ratio unit is directly obtained using the formula (cy − dx) ÷ (ad − bc).

questions.question: A candy shop owner buys three kinds of candies: red, blue, and green. Red candies are purchased at 3 for ₹15, blue candies at 4 for ₹18, and green candies at 5 for ₹22. He mixes them in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. He sells all the mixed candies at 2 for ₹10. What is his approximate gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
CP per candy: Red = 15 ÷ 3 = ₹5, Blue = 18 ÷ 4 = ₹4.5, Green = 22 ÷ 5 = ₹4.4
Total CP for 4 mixed candies (in ratio 1:1:2) = 5 + 4.5 + (2 × 4.4) = ₹18.3
SP for 4 mixed candies = 4 × (10 ÷ 2) = ₹20
Profit = 20 − 18.3 = ₹1.7
Profit % = (1.7 ÷ 18.3) × 100 ≈ 9.29%
∴ The correct answer is Profit of 9.29%.

Alternate Method
Candy Mixture (1 : 1 : 2 Ratio)
1 Red @ ₹5
1 Blue @ ₹4.5
2 Green @ ₹4.4
Total CP = ₹18.3
+ Profit ₹1.7
Total SP = ₹20
Profit % = (1.7 ÷ 18.3) × 100 ≈ 9.29%

Given:
Red candies bought at 3 for ₹15

Blue candies bought at 4 for ₹18

Green candies bought at 5 for ₹22

Mixture ratio = 1 : 1 : 2
Selling price = 2 for ₹10

Calculations:
⇒ Let the number of Red, Blue, and Green candies mixed be 1, 1, and 2 respectively.
⇒ Total candies mixed = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 candies
⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 Red candy = 15 ÷ 3 = ₹5
⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 Blue candy = 18 ÷ 4 = ₹4.5
⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 Green candy = 22 ÷ 5 = ₹4.4
⇒ Total Cost Price of 4 mixed candies = (1 × 5) + (1 × 4.5) + (2 × 4.4)
⇒ Total CP = 5 + 4.5 + 8.8 = ₹18.3
⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 1 candy = 10 ÷ 2 = ₹5
⇒ Total SP of 4 mixed candies = 4 × 5 = ₹20
⇒ Since SP is greater than CP, there is a profit.
⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 20 − 18.3 = ₹1.7
⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100
⇒ Profit % = (1.7 ÷ 18.3) × 100
⇒ Profit % = 170 ÷ 18.3 ≈ 9.289% ≈ 9.29%
∴ The correct answer is Profit of 9.29%.

Additional Information
Profit & Loss Formulas

Profit occurs when Selling Price (SP) > Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP. Profit Percentage is calculated on the total Cost Price: (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Mixture Average Cost

When different quantities of items are mixed, the Average Cost Price is simply the total cost of all components combined, divided by the total physical quantity.

Ratio Multipliers Trick

Instead of finding a large common multiple (LCM) to equate quantities, directly taking sample quantities equal to the given ratio (such as 1, 1, and 2 units) makes percentage-based calculations perfectly proportional and much faster.

questions.question: A 100-litre solution contains acid and water in the ratio 3:2. Some quantity of this solution is removed and replaced with pure acid. If the final ratio of acid to water becomes 7:3, how many litres of solution were replaced?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Apply the alligation method on the water concentration of the mixtures.

Initial mixture water = 40%, Added pure acid water = 0%, Final mixture water = 30%.
Ratio of remaining mixture to added pure acid = (30 − 0) : (40 − 30) = 30 : 10 = 3 : 1.
This means 1 part out of a total of (3 + 1) = 4 parts was replaced.
Replaced quantity = 1 / 4 of total volume = (1 / 4) × 100 = 25 litres.
∴ The correct answer is 25 litres.

Alternate Method
Given:
Initial volume of the solution = 100 litres
Initial ratio of acid to water = 3 : 2
Final ratio of acid to water = 7 : 3

Calculations:
⇒ Quantity of water in the initial solution = (2 / 5) × 100 = 40 litres
⇒ Let x litres of the solution be removed and replaced with pure acid.
⇒ Quantity of water removed = (2 / 5) × x = 0.4x litres
⇒ Remaining water in the solution = 40 − 0.4x litres
⇒ Since only pure acid is added back, the overall quantity of water in the final mixture does not increase.
⇒ Final volume of the solution is maintained at 100 litres.
⇒ Quantity of water in the final solution = (3 / 10) × 100 = 30 litres
⇒ Equating the remaining water to final water:
⇒ 40 − 0.4x = 30
⇒ 0.4x = 10
⇒ x = 10 ÷ 0.4 = 25 litres
∴ The correct answer is 25 litres.

questions.question: A circular park having a radius of 14 m. If a 1.5 m wide path is built around it, what is the approximate area of the path?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Area of a circular path outside a circle = π × w × (2r + w)
Area = (22 ÷ 7) × 1.5 × (2 × 14 + 1.5)
Area = (33 ÷ 7) × 29.5 = 973.5 ÷ 7 ≈ 139.07 m²
∴ The correct answer is 139 m².

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Radius of the circular park, r = 14 m
⇒ Width of the path built around it, w = 1.5 m

Formula Used:
⇒ Area of the path = Area of the outer circle − Area of the inner circle
⇒ Area of a circle = πR²

Calculations:
⇒ Outer radius, R = r + w
⇒ R = 14 + 1.5 = 15.5 m
⇒ Area of the path = πR² − πr²
⇒ Area = π × (15.5² − 14²)
⇒ Area = (22 ÷ 7) × (15.5 + 14) × (15.5 − 14)
⇒ Area = (22 ÷ 7) × 29.5 × 1.5
⇒ Area = (33 ÷ 7) × 29.5
⇒ Area = 973.5 ÷ 7 ≈ 139.07 m²
⇒ The approximate area of the path is 139 m².
∴ The correct answer is 139 m².

questions.question: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 21 horses in the field for 6 months and 15 cows for 2 months. B adds 15 cows for 6 months and 40 sheep for 7.5 months. If 3 horses consume the same amount of food as 5 cows, and 6 cows eat as much as 10 sheep, what portion of the rent should A cover?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert all animals to equivalent cows to find the total grazing units.

1 horse = 5/3 cows and 1 sheep = 3/5 cows.
A's total grazing = (21 × 5/3 × 6) + (15 × 2) = 210 + 30 = 240 cow-months.
B's total grazing = (15 × 6) + (40 × 3/5 × 7.5) = 90 + 180 = 270 cow-months.
A's rent portion = 240 ÷ (240 + 270) = 240 ÷ 510 = 8/17.
∴ The correct answer is 8/17.

Alternate Method
Given:
A places 21 horses for 6 months and 15 cows for 2 months.

B places 15 cows for 6 months and 40 sheep for 7.5 months.

Food equality: 3 horses = 5 cows and 6 cows = 10 sheep.

Formula Used:
Total Usage = Equivalent Number of Animals × Time Period

240 Units
Ratio: 8
270 Units
Ratio: 9
A's Rent Share
B's Rent Share

Calculations:
⇒ First, convert all animals into equivalent cow units for calculation consistency.
⇒ 3 horses = 5 cows ⇒ 1 horse = 5/3 cows
⇒ 6 cows = 10 sheep ⇒ 1 sheep = 6/10 = 3/5 cows
⇒ Total grazing consumption for A = (21 × 5/3 × 6) + (15 × 2)
⇒ Total equivalent units for A = 210 + 30 = 240 cow-months
⇒ Total grazing consumption for B = (15 × 6) + (40 × 3/5 × 7.5)
⇒ Total equivalent units for B = 90 + 180 = 270 cow-months
⇒ The total rent will be distributed in the ratio of their total grazing consumption.
⇒ Ratio of rent share (A : B) = 240 : 270 = 8 : 9
⇒ Total ratio parts = 8 + 9 = 17 parts
⇒ Portion of the rent A should cover = 8 / 17
∴ The correct answer is 8/17.

questions.question: Two individuals, A and B rent a pasture. A uses 16 cows for a duration of 3 months and 20 sheep for 4 months and B uses 30 sheep for 6 months. If 4 cows are equivalent to 8 sheep, determine A's portion of the rent.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert cows to equivalent sheep: 4 cows = 8 sheep ⇒ 1 cow = 2 sheep.
A's equivalent sheep-months = (16 × 2 × 3) + (20 × 4) = 96 + 80 = 176.
B's equivalent sheep-months = 30 × 6 = 180.
Ratio of A's rent to B's rent = 176 : 180 = 44 : 45.
A's portion out of the total rent = 44 ÷ (44 + 45) = 44/89.
∴ The correct answer is 44/89.

Alternate Method
Given:
A uses 16 cows for 3 months and 20 sheep for 4 months.

B uses 30 sheep for 6 months.

Equivalence: 4 cows = 8 sheep.

Formula Used:
Rent Share Ratio = Total equivalent animal-months of A : Total equivalent animal-months of B

Rent Sharing Proportion
A: 176 units
B: 180 units
Ratio = 44
Ratio = 45

Calculations:
⇒ First, find the sheep equivalent for A's cows.
⇒ 4 cows = 8 sheep → 1 cow = 2 sheep.
⇒ A's 16 cows = 16 × 2 = 32 sheep.
⇒ Total equivalent sheep-months for A = (32 sheep × 3 months) + (20 sheep × 4 months).
⇒ Total for A = 96 + 80 = 176 sheep-months.
⇒ Total equivalent sheep-months for B = 30 sheep × 6 months.
⇒ Total for B = 180 sheep-months.
⇒ Rent Ratio (A : B) = 176 : 180 = 44 : 45.
⇒ Total proportion parts = 44 + 45 = 89.
⇒ A's portion of the rent = 44/89.
∴ The correct answer is 44/89.

questions.question: How many approximate kgs of sugar costing ₹45 per kg must be mixed with 25 kg of sugar costing ₹32 per kg so that a 15% gain may be obtained by selling the mixture at ₹43.70 per kg?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
First, find the Cost Price (CP) of the mixture from its Selling Price (SP) and Gain %.

CP of mixture = SP ÷ (1 + Gain%) = 43.70 ÷ 1.15 = ₹38/kg
Using Alligation, Ratio of quantities = (38 − 32) : (45 − 38) = 6 : 7

Since 7 parts correspond to 25 kg, 6 parts will correspond to: (25 ÷ 7) × 6 = 150 ÷ 7 ≈ 21.43 kg

∴ The correct answer is 21 kg.

Alternate Method
Given:
CP of first type of sugar = ₹45/kg
CP of second type of sugar = ₹32/kg
Quantity of second type of sugar = 25 kg
SP of mixture = ₹43.70/kg
Profit on mixture = 15%

Calculations:
⇒ Mean CP of mixture = 43.70 × [100 ÷ (100 + 15)]
⇒ Mean CP = (43.70 × 100) ÷ 115
⇒ Mean CP = 4370 ÷ 115 = ₹38/kg
⇒ Using the rule of alligation, the ratio of the quantities is:
⇒ (Mean CP − CP2) : (CP1 − Mean CP) = (38 − 32) : (45 − 38) = 6 : 7
⇒ Let the required quantity of the first type of sugar be x kg.
⇒ x ÷ 25 = 6 ÷ 7
⇒ x = (25 × 6) ÷ 7
⇒ x = 150 ÷ 7 ≈ 21.43 kg
⇒ Therefore, approximately 21 kg of the first type of sugar must be mixed.
∴ The correct answer is 21 kg.

questions.question: In a city, the current number of literate people is 25,000. If the number of literate males decreases by 5% and the number of literate females increases by 10%, the total literate population becomes 25,250. What is the present number of literate males in the city?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Net increase in population = 25250 − 25000 = 250.
Overall percentage change = (250 ÷ 25000) × 100 = +1%.

Using the Alligation method on the percentage change of Males (−5%) and Females (+10%):

Ratio of Males to Females = (10 − 1) : (1 − (−5)) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2.
Present number of literate males = (3 ÷ 5) × 25000 = 15000.
∴ The correct answer is 15,000 males.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total current literate population = 25,000
New total literate population = 25,250
Net increase = 25,250 − 25,000 = 250

Calculations:
Let the current number of literate males be M and females be F.
⇒ M + F = 25,000 --- (Equation 1)

The number of males decreases by 5% and females increases by 10%, resulting in a net increase of 250.

⇒ 10% of F − 5% of M = 250
⇒ (10 ÷ 100) × F − (5 ÷ 100) × M = 250

Multiplying the entire equation by 100:

⇒ 10F − 5M = 25,000

Dividing by 5 to simplify:

⇒ 2F − M = 5,000 --- (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (M + F) + (2F − M) = 25,000 + 5,000
⇒ 3F = 30,000
⇒ F = 10,000

Substituting the value of F back into Equation 1:

⇒ M + 10,000 = 25,000
⇒ M = 15,000
∴ The correct answer is 15,000 males.

questions.question: Evaluate the expression: \(\left(\frac{1}{3-\sqrt{8}}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{7}}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{6}}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{5}}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}\right) = ?\)
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Rewrite 3 as √9 and 2 as √4 to see the continuous pattern.

Rationalizing 1/(√a − √b) gives √a + √b when a − b = 1.
The given expression evaluates to: (√9 + √8) − (√8 + √7) + (√7 + √6) − (√6 + √5) + (√5 + √4)

All intermediate terms cancel out, leaving only the first and last parts: √9 + √4 = 3 + 2 = 5

∴ The correct answer is 5.

Alternate Method
Given:
1/(3 − √8) − 1/(√8 − √7) + 1/(√7 − √6) − 1/(√6 − √5) + 1/(√5 − 2)

Formula Used:
(a − b)(a + b) = a^2 − b^2

Calculations:
⇒ Rationalize the first term:
⇒ 1/(3 − √8) = (3 + √8) / (3^2 − (√8)^2) = (3 + √8) / (9 − 8) = 3 + √8
⇒ Rationalize the second term:
⇒ 1/(√8 − √7) = (√8 + √7) / ((√8)^2 − (√7)^2) = (√8 + √7) / (8 − 7) = √8 + √7
⇒ Rationalize the third term:
⇒ 1/(√7 − √6) = (√7 + √6) / (7 − 6) = √7 + √6
⇒ Rationalize the fourth term:
⇒ 1/(√6 − √5) = (√6 + √5) / (6 − 5) = √6 + √5
⇒ Rationalize the fifth term:
⇒ 1/(√5 − 2) = (√5 + 2) / ((√5)^2 − 2^2) = (√5 + 2) / (5 − 4) = √5 + 2
⇒ Substitute all these simplified values back into the original expression:
⇒ (3 + √8) − (√8 + √7) + (√7 + √6) − (√6 + √5) + (√5 + 2)
⇒ Expand by applying the minus signs:
⇒ 3 + √8 − √8 − √7 + √7 + √6 − √6 − √5 + √5 + 2
⇒ Cancel out the opposite matching pairs:
⇒ 3 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 2 = 5
∴ The correct answer is 5.

Additional Information
Rationalization of Surds

To remove a square root surd from the denominator, multiply both the numerator and denominator by its conjugate. The conjugate of (√a − √b) is (√a + √b).

Difference of Squares Formula
The standard algebraic identity (x − y)(x + y) = x^2 − y^2 is widely applied during rationalization to eliminate square root symbols entirely from denominators.

Continuous Series Simplification

When solving a continuous sequence of surd fractions, locating patterns like differences of 1 will allow quick cancellation of intermediate terms, drastically reducing calculation time.

questions.question: The average of 13 numbers is 70. The average of the first five numbers is 60. The average of the next five numbers is 25% higher than the average of the first five numbers. The 11th number is 6 less than the 13th number, and the 12th number is 4 greater than the 13th number. What is the average of the 11th and 12th numbers?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Net deviation of the first 10 numbers from the overall average 70 = 5 × (60 − 70) + 5 × (75 − 70) = −50 + 25 = −25.

To balance the overall average, the sum of the last 3 numbers must be = 3 × 70 − (−25) = 235.

Let the 13th number be x. Then 11th = x − 6, and 12th = x + 4.
Sum = (x − 6) + (x + 4) + x = 3x − 2 = 235 ⇒ x = 79.
The 11th number = 73, and the 12th number = 83. Their average = (73 + 83) ÷ 2 = 78.
∴ The correct answer is 78.

Alternate Method
Given:
Average of 13 numbers = 70
Average of first 5 numbers = 60
Average of next 5 numbers = 60 + (25% of 60) = 75
11th number = 13th number − 6
12th number = 13th number + 4

1st 5 Nums
Avg: 60
Sum: 300
Next 5 Nums
Avg: 75
Sum: 375
11th, 12th, 13th
Avg: ?
Sum: 235
Total Sum of 13 Nums = 910 (Avg = 70)

Formula Used:
Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

Calculations:
⇒ Total sum of 13 numbers = 13 × 70 = 910
⇒ Sum of first 5 numbers = 5 × 60 = 300
⇒ Sum of next 5 numbers = 5 × 75 = 375
⇒ Sum of the remaining 3 numbers (11th, 12th, 13th) = 910 − (300 + 375) = 235
⇒ Let the 13th number be x.
⇒ 11th number = x − 6
⇒ 12th number = x + 4
⇒ Sum of these three numbers = (x − 6) + (x + 4) + x = 3x − 2
⇒ 3x − 2 = 235
⇒ 3x = 237
⇒ x = 79
⇒ 11th number = 79 − 6 = 73
⇒ 12th number = 79 + 4 = 83
⇒ Average of 11th and 12th numbers = (73 + 83) ÷ 2 = 156 ÷ 2 = 78
∴ The correct answer is 78.

Additional Information
Weighted Average

When different groups have different averages, the combined average is calculated as (n1A1 + n2A2 + ...) ÷ (n1 + n2 + ...).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. This property is highly useful for finding missing observations in a data set without calculating heavy sum values.

Successive Percentage Increase

If a base value is increased by x%, the new value is obtained by multiplying the base by (1 + x/100). For example, a 25% increase on a base of 60 makes it 60 × 1.25 = 75.

questions.question: If the compound interest on a certain sum at 16(2/3)% per annum for 3 years is ₹1270, find the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate and for the same period.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Rate = 16 2/3% = 1/6.
Let Principal = 6^3 = 216 units.
Amount after 3 years = 7^3 = 343 units ⇒ CI = 343 − 216 = 127 units.
Given CI = ₹1270 ⇒ 127 units = 1270 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹10.
SI for 3 years = 216 × (1/6) × 3 = 108 units = 108 × 10 = ₹1080.
∴ The correct answer is ₹1080.

questions.question: An antique dealer sold three items, A, B, and C, with their selling prices in the ratio 4:5:6. He suffered a loss of 10% on item A, made a profit of 50% on item B, and broke even (no profit, no loss) on item C. What was his approximate percentage gain or loss in the overall deal?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
To avoid decimal calculations, multiply the SP ratio 4 : 5 : 6 by 9 to get assumed SP values: 36, 45, and 54.
Total SP = 36 + 45 + 54 = 135 units.
CP of A = 36 ÷ 0.90 = 40, CP of B = 45 ÷ 1.50 = 30, and CP of C = 54 (no profit/loss).
Total CP = 40 + 30 + 54 = 124 units.
Profit = 135 − 124 = 11 units. ⇒ Profit % = (11 ÷ 124) × 100 ≈ 8.87% (approx. 8.88%).
∴ The correct answer is profit of 8.88%.

questions.question: A wholesaler buys a batch of ceiling fans at a 50% markup over the factory's base cost ₹C. He then allows a 20% trade discount to the retailer. The retailer applies a 40% markup on his cost and offers a flat 10% discount to customers on the printed price. If a customer finally pays ₹18,144, what is the original base cost (₹C) of one ceiling fan from the factory?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Applying successive percentage multipliers on the base cost C yields the final selling price:

Final SP = C × 1.5 (markup) × 0.8 (discount) × 1.4 (markup) × 0.9 (discount)
⇒ 18144 = C × 1.2 × 1.26
⇒ 18144 = 1.512C
⇒ C = 18144 ÷ 1.512 = 12000
∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.

questions.question: A circular pond is surrounded by a path 2 m wide. If the total area (pond + path) is 616 m² and the pond area is 452.16 m², what is the radius of the pond? (take π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
The area of the pond is directly given as 452.16 m².
Area of a circular pond = π × r²
⇒ 3.14 × r² = 452.16
⇒ r² = 452.16 ÷ 3.14 = 144
⇒ r = √144 = 12 m
∴ The correct answer is 12 m.

questions.question: Given, x + 1/x = 5, then determine the value of x² + 1/x².
questions.solution:
If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.
Here, k = 5.
x² + 1/x² = 5² − 2 = 25 − 2 = 23
∴ The correct answer is 23.

questions.question: A and B share a rented field. A utilizes 20 horses for 5 months, while B uses 30 cows for 4 months and 45 sheep for 5 months. If 2 horses are equivalent to 5 cows, and 3 cows are equal to 9 sheep. What portion of the rent is A pay?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Convert all animals into equivalent cows: 1 horse = 2.5 cows, and 3 sheep = 1 cow.
A's usage = (20 × 2.5) cows × 5 months = 250 cow-months.
B's usage = (30 cows × 4 months) + (45 ÷ 3) cows × 5 months = 120 + 75 = 195 cow-months.
Total equivalent usage = 250 + 195 = 445 cow-months.
A's rent portion = A's usage ÷ Total usage = 250 ÷ 445 = 50/89.
∴ The correct answer is 50/89.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ A uses 20 horses for 5 months.
⇒ B uses 30 cows for 4 months and 45 sheep for 5 months.
⇒ Conversion rates: 2 horses = 5 cows, and 3 cows = 9 sheep.

Formula Used:
⇒ Portion of Rent = (Individual Equivalent Usage) ÷ (Total Equivalent Usage)

Equivalent Cow-Months Usage
A: 250 units
B: 195 units
Share: 250 / 445 = 50 / 89
Share: 195 / 445 = 39 / 89

Calculations:
⇒ Determine equivalent cow units for A:
⇒ 2 horses = 5 cows ⇒ 20 horses = (5 ÷ 2) × 20 = 50 cows.
⇒ A's total usage = 50 cows × 5 months = 250 cow-months.
⇒ Determine equivalent cow units for B:
⇒ 9 sheep = 3 cows ⇒ 45 sheep = (3 ÷ 9) × 45 = 15 cows.
⇒ B's usage from cows = 30 cows × 4 months = 120 cow-months.
⇒ B's usage from sheep = 15 cows × 5 months = 75 cow-months.
⇒ B's total usage = 120 + 75 = 195 cow-months.
⇒ Total usage by A and B = 250 + 195 = 445 cow-months.
⇒ A's portion = 250 ÷ 445.
⇒ Simplify the fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by 5:
⇒ 250 ÷ 5 = 50
⇒ 445 ÷ 5 = 89
⇒ A's Portion = 50/89
∴ The correct answer is 50/89.

Additional Information
Partnership in Renting

When individuals share a rented property or field, the rent must be divided proportionally based on both the amount of resources used and the time duration (Usage × Time).

Animal Equivalence

When multiple entity types are involved (horses, cows, sheep), convert all of them into a single common base unit before calculating the total usage to ensure a uniform scale.

Compound Ratio

The final ratio of share is a compound ratio formed by multiplying the equivalent units ratio and the time ratio for each individual.

questions.question: A and B start a business. A invests 2 times more than B. After 8 months, A withdraws half of his capital, and B triples his capital. If the total profit after one year is ₹75,000, find the share of A.
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
A invests 2 times more than B ⇒ Initial capital ratio A : B = 3 : 1.
A's profit units = (3 × 8) + (1.5 × 4) = 30; B's profit units = (1 × 8) + (3 × 4) = 20.
Profit ratio A : B = 30 : 20 = 3 : 2.
A's share = [3 ÷ (3 + 2)] × 75000 = ₹45,000.
∴ The correct answer is ₹45,000.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Total profit after one year (12 months) = ₹75,000
⇒ A invests 2 times more than B initially.

Formula Used:
⇒ Profit Ratio = (Capital × Time)

A
8 mo × 3x
4 mo × 1.5x
Sum = 30x
B
8 mo × 1x
4 mo × 3x
Sum = 20x
Profit Ratio (A : B) = 30x : 20x = 3 : 2

Calculations:
⇒ Let B's initial investment be x.
⇒ A invests 2 times more than B, so A's initial investment = x + 2x = 3x.
⇒ For the first 8 months, A's capital is 3x and B's capital is x.
⇒ For the remaining 4 months, A withdraws half of his capital, so A's new capital = 3x ÷ 2 = 1.5x.
⇒ For the remaining 4 months, B triples his capital, so B's new capital = 3 × x = 3x.
⇒ A's profit equivalent = (3x × 8) + (1.5x × 4) = 24x + 6x = 30x.
⇒ B's profit equivalent = (x × 8) + (3x × 4) = 8x + 12x = 20x.
⇒ Profit Ratio of A : B = 30x : 20x = 3 : 2.
⇒ Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5 parts.
⇒ A's share = (3 ÷ 5) × 75000 = 3 × 15000
⇒ A's share = ₹45,000.
∴ The correct answer is ₹45,000.

Additional Information
Partnership Core Principle

Profit is exclusively distributed among partners in the ratio of their effective investments (the product of capital and duration). Key formula: Profit Ratio = C1T1 : C2T2.

"More Than" Phrasing Concept

When a question states "A is n times more than B", the expression evaluates to A = B + nB. It must not be confused with "A is n times of B" which simply means A = nB.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An active partner actively works for the business and typically claims a salary or fixed percentage of total profit before the remainder is split purely based on the initial capital-time ratio among all partners.

questions.question: A stationery supplier ordered 8 boxes of premium pens and some boxes of standard pens. The price of premium pens per box was twice that of standard pens. When the order was delivered, the number of boxes of premium and standard pens had been accidentally interchanged. This increased the total bill by 25%. What was the ratio of the original number of boxes of premium pens to the original number of boxes of standard pens?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
Let the price of standard and premium pens be 1 and 2 units respectively, and standard boxes ordered be y.

Original Cost = (8 × 2) + (y × 1) = 16 + y
New Cost (after interchange) = (y × 2) + (8 × 1) = 2y + 8

Given a 25% increase in the bill, the multiplier is 5/4, giving: (2y + 8) / (16 + y) = 5 / 4

⇒ 8y + 32 = 5y + 80 ⇒ 3y = 48 ⇒ y = 16
Ratio of Premium to Standard = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2.
∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Alternate Method
Given:
Original number of premium boxes = 8

Price of a premium box is twice the price of a standard box.

New total bill is 25% more than the original bill due to interchanged quantities.

Original Bill (100%)
16 + y
New Bill (125%)
2y + 8
+ 25% Increase

Calculations:
⇒ Let the original number of standard pen boxes be y and price per standard box be P.
⇒ Price per premium box = 2P.
⇒ Original Bill = (8 × 2P) + (y × P) = P(16 + y)
⇒ When quantities are interchanged, there are y premium boxes and 8 standard boxes.
⇒ New Bill = (y × 2P) + (8 × P) = P(2y + 8)
⇒ The new bill is 25% more than the original, so New Bill = 1.25 × Original Bill
⇒ P(2y + 8) = 1.25 × P(16 + y)
⇒ 2y + 8 = 1.25 × (16 + y)
⇒ 2y + 8 = 20 + 1.25y
⇒ 2y − 1.25y = 20 − 8
⇒ 0.75y = 12
⇒ y = 12 ÷ 0.75 = 16
⇒ Original number of standard pen boxes = 16.
⇒ Required ratio (Premium boxes : Standard boxes) = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2.
∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.

Additional Information
Ratio & Proportion

A ratio compares values, showing how much of one there is compared to another. If two quantities are in the ratio a:b, they can be represented directly as ax and bx for calculation purposes to quickly establish a relation.

Percentage Increase

When a quantity increases by R%, its new value becomes (100 + R)% of the original. An increase of 25% corresponds to a multiplying factor of 125% or 5/4.

Interchange of Quantities

When two items with original quantities x and y and respective unit prices a and b are interchanged, the net change in the total bill follows the shortcut formula: Change = (a − b)(y − x). A positive result directly indicates a percentage increase.

questions.question: A furniture manufacturer sells a dining table set to a showroom at a 25% discount on the marked price, but adds a 10% handling fee on the discounted price. The showroom then sells the set for ₹4500 more than what they paid, thereby earning a profit of 30%. At what price had the manufacturer marked the dining table set?
questions.solution: Cost Price (CP) for the showroom = Profit ÷ Profit% = 4500 ÷ 30% = ₹15,000. Net multiplying factor from MP to CP = (1 − 25%) × (1 + 10%) = 0.75 × 1.10 = 0.825. Marked Price (MP) = CP ÷ Net Factor = 15,000 ÷ 0.825 = 2,00,000 ÷ 11 ≈ ₹18,181.82.

questions.question: A school organized a field trip for 100 students and 10 chaperones. Each student was given a snack pack containing items equal to 15% of the total number of students. Each chaperone received a snack pack with items equal to 25% of the total number of students. How many snack items were distributed in total?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Total items for students = 100 × (15% of 100) = 100 × 15 = 1500
Total items for chaperones = 10 × (25% of 100) = 10 × 25 = 250
Total items distributed = 1500 + 250 = 1750
∴ The correct answer is 1750 items.

Alternate Method
Given:
Total number of students = 100
Total number of chaperones = 10
Items per student's snack pack = 15% of total students
Items per chaperone's snack pack = 25% of total students

Formula Used:
Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Base Value

Students
Count = 100
Items/pack = 15% of 100 = 15
Total = 100 × 15 = 1500
+
Chaperones
Count = 10
Items/pack = 25% of 100 = 25
Total = 10 × 25 = 250
Total Snack Items = 1500 + 250 = 1750

Calculations:
⇒ Items in each student's pack = 15% of 100 = (15 ÷ 100) × 100 = 15 items
⇒ Total items given to 100 students = 100 × 15 = 1500 items
⇒ Items in each chaperone's pack = 25% of 100 = (25 ÷ 100) × 100 = 25 items
⇒ Total items given to 10 chaperones = 10 × 25 = 250 items
⇒ Total items distributed = Total student items + Total chaperone items
⇒ Total items distributed = 1500 + 250 = 1750
∴ The correct answer is 1750 items.

questions.question: A clothing store sold three dresses, D1, D2, and D3, whose selling prices were in the ratio 5:6:7. They made a profit of 20% on D1, a loss of 10% on D2, and a profit of 30% on D3. What was their approximate total profit or loss percentage for the entire sale?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Let SP of dresses D1, D2, and D3 be 5, 6, and 7 units respectively. (Total SP = 18)

Since profit is 20%, loss is 10%, and profit is 30% respectively, their multipliers are 1.2, 0.9, and 1.3.

Total CP = 5/1.2 + 6/0.9 + 7/1.3 = 25/6 + 20/3 + 70/13 = 65/6 + 70/13 = 1265/78
Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP = 18 − 1265/78 = 139/78
Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100 = (139/78 ÷ 1265/78) × 100 = 13900/1265 ≈ 10.98%
∴ The correct answer is profit of 10.98%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Selling Price (SP) ratio of D1 : D2 : D3 = 5 : 6 : 7
Profit on D1 = 20%, Loss on D2 = 10%, Profit on D3 = 30%

Formula Used:
Cost Price (CP) = [SP ÷ (100 ± Profit/Loss %)] × 100
Overall Profit % = [(Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP] × 100

Calculations:
Let the Selling Prices of the three dresses be 500, 600, and 700 units respectively.

⇒ Total SP = 500 + 600 + 700 = 1800 units

Calculating the Cost Price of each dress:

⇒ CP of D1 = (500 ÷ 120) × 100 = 5000/12 = 1250/3 units
⇒ CP of D2 = (600 ÷ 90) × 100 = 6000/9 = 2000/3 units
⇒ CP of D3 = (700 ÷ 130) × 100 = 7000/13 units
⇒ Total CP = 1250/3 + 2000/3 + 7000/13
⇒ Total CP = 3250/3 + 7000/13 = (42250 + 21000) ÷ 39 = 63250/39 units
Now, finding the overall profit margin:
⇒ Total SP = 1800 = 70200/39 units
⇒ Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP = (70200 − 63250) ÷ 39 = 6950/39 units
⇒ Profit % = [(6950/39) ÷ (63250/39)] × 100
⇒ Profit % = (6950 ÷ 63250) × 100
⇒ Profit % = (695 ÷ 6325) × 100 = (139 ÷ 1265) × 100 ≈ 10.988%
∴ The correct answer is profit of 10.98%.

questions.question: A wholesaler marks up the price of a microwave oven by 60% above its cost price. He gives a 15% trade discount to a retailer. The retailer, in turn, marks up the price by 25% above his purchase price and offers a 10% festival discount to the customer. If the customer finally pays ₹14,490 for the microwave, what is the original approximate cost price of the oven to the wholesaler?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
In successive chain transactions, the equivalent multiplying factor method is the fastest.

Net multiplying factor = 1.60 (wholesaler markup) × 0.85 (wholesaler discount) × 1.25 (retailer markup) × 0.90 (retailer discount)
Net factor = 1.60 × 0.85 × 1.25 × 0.90 = 1.53
14490 = Original CP × 1.53 ⇒ CP = 14490 ÷ 1.53 ≈ 9470.588
∴ The correct answer is ₹9,471.

Alternate Method
Wholesaler
CP = 100x
Wholesaler
MP = 160x
Retailer
CP = 136x
Retailer
MP = 170x
Final
SP = 153x
+60%
−15%
+25%
−10%
Final SP = 153x = ₹14,490

Given:
Final Selling Price (paid by customer) = ₹14,490
Let the original cost price of the microwave to the wholesaler be 100x.

Calculations:
⇒ Wholesaler's Marked Price (MP) = 100x + 60% of 100x = 160x
⇒ Trade discount given by wholesaler = 15% of 160x = 24x
⇒ Retailer's Cost Price (CP) = 160x − 24x = 136x
⇒ Retailer's Marked Price (MP) = 136x + 25% of 136x = 136x + 34x = 170x
⇒ Festival discount given by retailer = 10% of 170x = 17x
⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) = 170x − 17x = 153x
⇒ According to the given data, Final SP = 14490
⇒ 153x = 14490
⇒ x = 14490 ÷ 153 ≈ 94.7058
⇒ Wholesaler's Cost Price = 100x = 100 × 94.7058 = 9470.58
⇒ Approximate original cost price = ₹9,471
∴ The correct answer is ₹9,471.

questions.question: A and B can complete a task together in 12 days, while B and C can finish it in 16 days. After A works on it for 5 days and B for 7 days, C takes the remaining 13 days to finish the work. How many days would it take for C to complete the work alone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Total Work = LCM(12, 16) = 48 units. Efficiency: (A + B) = 4, (B + C) = 3.
Given: A works 5 days, B works 7 days, C works 13 days = Total Work.
Rewrite as: 5(A + B) + 2(B + C) + 11C = 48 units.
⇒ 5(4) + 2(3) + 11C = 48 ⇒ 26 + 11C = 48 ⇒ C = 2 units/day.
Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 days.
∴ The correct answer is 24 days.

questions.question:
Two individuals, X and Y, rent a pasture together. X has 10 goats that they graze for 3 months. Y grazes 15 sheep for 4 months and 5 horses for 2 months. The following relationships are given:
2 goats are equivalent to 3 sheep, 1 sheep is equivalent to 2 horses.
What amount of rent should X pay if the total rent is split by grazing units?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Convert all animals to Sheep Units: 1 Goat = 1.5 Sheep and 1 Horse = 0.5 Sheep.
X units = 10 Goats × 1.5 × 3 Months = 45.
Y units = (15 Sheep × 4 Months) + (5 Horses × 0.5 × 2 Months) = 60 + 5 = 65.
X share = 45 ÷ (45 + 65) = 45 ÷ 110 = 9/22.
∴ The correct answer is 9/22.

Alternate Method
Given:
X: 10 Goats for 3 Months.
Y: 15 Sheep for 4 Months and 5 Horses for 2 Months.
Equivalency: 2 Goats = 3 Sheep; 1 Sheep = 2 Horses.

Conversion to Sheep Units:

⇒ 1 Goat = 3/2 Sheep = 1.5 Sheep
⇒ 1 Horse = 1/2 Sheep = 0.5 Sheep

Calculating Total Consumption:

⇒ X Consumption = (10 × 1.5) × 3 = 15 × 3 = 45 Unit-months
⇒ Y Consumption = (15 × 4) + (5 × 0.5 × 2) = 60 + 5 = 65 Unit-months

Rent Calculation:

⇒ Total Rent Units = 45 + 65 = 110 Units
⇒ X Share = X Units ÷ Total Units
⇒ X Share = 45/110 = 9/22
∴ The correct answer is 9/22.

Additional Information
Partnership Concept

In a joint venture or rental, the cost is shared in the ratio of (Investment/Quantity × Time). Profit or rent share ∝ (Q × T).

Equivalent Units

When different entities are involved, always convert all quantities into a single common base unit using the given equivalence ratios before performing calculations.

Ratio and Proportion

If a total W is divided in the ratio a : b, then the share of the first person is a / (a + b) × W.

questions.question: P, Q, and R started a business with capitals in the ratio 1:2:3. After 4 months, R withdrew 50% of his capital. After another 4 months, Q withdrew 25% of his capital. The business continued for a total of 12 months. Find the ratio of profit shares of P : Q : R.
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Let initial capitals of P, Q, and R be 1, 2, and 3 units.
P's share = 1 × 12 = 12 units.
Q's share = (2 × 8 months) + (1.5 × 4 months) = 16 + 6 = 22 units.
R's share = (3 × 4 months) + (1.5 × 8 months) = 12 + 12 = 24 units.
Required Ratio = 12 : 22 : 24 = 6 : 11 : 12.
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 11 : 12.

Alternate Method
Given: Initial capital ratio P : Q : R = 1 : 2 : 3. Total duration = 12 months.
Formula: Profit Share = Capital × Time

Step-by-step calculation:

⇒ Let capitals of P, Q, and R be x, 2x, and 3x.
⇒ Profit of P = x × 12 = 12x
⇒ Profit of Q = (2x × 8) + (2x − 25% of 2x) × 4
⇒ Profit of Q = 16x + (1.5x × 4) = 16x + 6x = 22x
⇒ Profit of R = (3x × 4) + (3x − 50% of 3x) × 8
⇒ Profit of R = 12x + (1.5x × 8) = 12x + 12x = 24x
⇒ Ratio P : Q : R = 12x : 22x : 24x
⇒ Dividing by 2x: Ratio = 6 : 11 : 12
∴ The correct answer is 6 : 11 : 12.

Additional Information
Partnership Rule

In a partnership, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of capital and time: P1 : P2 = (C1 × T1) : (C2 × T2).

Types of Partnership

Simple partnership involves same time periods for all, while compound partnership involves different time periods or changing capitals.

Working Partner

A partner who manages the business is a working partner and may receive a fixed salary or commission before the profit is shared.

questions.question: A fruit vendor buys three varieties of apples. The first variety is bought at 3 for 8, the second at 4 for 9, and the third at 1 for 4. He mixes them in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1 respectively. If he sells all the apples at 5 for 13, what is his approximate gain or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Take LCM of individual quantities (3, 4, 1) and selling quantity (5) = 60.

Assume mix ratio 1 : 2 : 1 as 60, 120, and 60 apples respectively.
Total Cost Price (CP) = (60 ÷ 3)×8 + (120 ÷ 4)×9 + (60 ÷ 1)×4 = 160 + 270 + 240 = ₹670.
Total Selling Price (SP) = (240 ÷ 5) × 13 = 48 × 13 = ₹624.
Loss % = [(670 − 624) ÷ 670] × 100 = (46 ÷ 670) × 100 ≈ 6.86%.
∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.8%.

Alternate Method
Given:
Variety 1: 3 apples for ₹8 | Variety 2: 4 apples for ₹9 | Variety 3: 1 apple for ₹4.
Mixing Ratio: 1 : 2 : 1 | Selling Price: 5 apples for ₹13.
Let the number of apples of each variety be 60, 120, and 60.
⇒ CP of Variety 1 = (8 ÷ 3) × 60 = ₹160.
⇒ CP of Variety 2 = (9 ÷ 4) × 120 = ₹270.
⇒ CP of Variety 3 = (4 ÷ 1) × 60 = ₹240.
⇒ Total Cost Price (CP) = 160 + 270 + 240 = ₹670.
⇒ Total Apples = 60 + 120 + 60 = 240 apples.
⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) = (13 ÷ 5) × 240 = ₹624.
⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 670 − 624 = ₹46.
⇒ Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (46 ÷ 670) × 100 = 6.865...%
∴ The correct answer is Loss of 6.8%.

Additional Information
Weighted Average CP

When multiple items with different rates are mixed, the net CP is (n1c1 + n2c2 + ...) ÷ (n1 + n2 + ...).

Profit and Loss Percentage
Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the CP.

Unitary Method for Quantities

To simplify calculations involving different quantities, assume a total quantity that is the LCM of all given denominators.

questions.question: A container holds a mixture of three liquids: A, B, and C, in the ratio of 4:3:1. 40 litres of this mixture are removed, and then 10 litres of liquid A and 15 litres of liquid B are poured into the container. If the resultant quantity of liquid B is 5 litres more than the resultant quantity of liquid A, what was the initial total quantity of the mixture in the container (in litres)?
questions.solution:
Solution
Shortcut Trick
Initial ratio of A:B:C = 4:3:1 ⇒ Total = 8 units.
In 40L removed, A = (4/8) × 40 = 20L and B = (3/8) × 40 = 15L.
Net change in A = −20 + 10 = −10L; Net change in B = −15 + 15 = 0L.
Let initial quantities be 4x and 3x. Resultant B − Resultant A = 5.
⇒ (3x + 0) − (4x − 10) = 5 ⇒ 10 − x = 5 ⇒ x = 5.
Initial mixture = 8x = 8 × 5 = 40 litres.
∴ The correct answer is 40 litres.

Alternate Method
Given: Initial ratio A:B:C = 4:3:1, Removed mixture = 40L, Added A = 10L, Added B = 15L, Final B − A = 5L.
Formula Used: Quantity of a component = (Ratio of component / Sum of ratios) × Total quantity.
Let the initial quantities of A, B, and C be 4x, 3x, and x respectively.
⇒ Initial total quantity = 4x + 3x + x = 8x.
⇒ Quantity of A removed = (4 / (4+3+1)) × 40 = (4/8) × 40 = 20 litres.
⇒ Quantity of B removed = (3 / 8) × 40 = 15 litres.
⇒ Resultant quantity of A = (4x − 20) + 10 = 4x − 10 litres.
⇒ Resultant quantity of B = (3x − 15) + 15 = 3x litres.
⇒ According to the condition: Resultant B − Resultant A = 5
⇒ 3x − (4x − 10) = 5
⇒ 3x − 4x + 10 = 5
⇒ −x = 5 − 10 ⇒ −x = −5 ⇒ x = 5.
⇒ Initial total quantity = 8x = 8 × 5 = 40 litres.
∴ The correct answer is 40 litres.

Additional Information
Mixture Ratio Invariance

When a portion of a mixture is removed, the ratio of the components in the remaining part as well as in the removed part remains the same as the original ratio.

Component Addition

Adding a pure component to a mixture only increases the quantity of that specific component and changes the overall ratio of the mixture.

Alligation Rule

For two-component mixtures, the Alligation method can be used to find the ratio in which two mixtures should be mixed to achieve a desired concentration.

questions.question: What is the average of all three-digit numbers divisible by 23?
questions.solution: The sequence of multiples forms an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.). Average of an A.P. = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2. First 3-digit multiple of 23 = 115. Last 3-digit multiple of 23 = 989. Average = (115 + 989) ÷ 2 = 552.

questions.question: A stationery shop ordered 6 dozen red pens and some additional dozen blue pens. The price of the red pens per dozen was three times that of the blue ones. When the order was delivered, it was found that the number of dozens of the two colours had been interchanged. This increased the bill by 40%. Find the ratio of the number of dozens of red pens to the number of dozens of blue pens in the original order.
questions.solution: Assume the price of Blue pens = 1 unit, Red pens = 3 units, and let Blue pens ordered = B dozens. Original Bill = (6 × 3) + (B × 1) = 18 + B. Interchanged Bill = (B × 3) + (6 × 1) = 3B + 6. The new bill is 40% more, meaning it is 1.4 times the original bill. ⇒ 3B + 6 = 1.4 × (18 + B) ⇒ 1.6B = 19.2 ⇒ B = 12. Required ratio = 6 : 12 = 1 : 2.

questions.question: A tank has a mixture of solutions A, B, and C in the respective ratio of 7:8:5. 40 litres of this mixture is drained out, and subsequently, 15 litres of solution A and 5 litres of solution C are added to the tank. If the resultant quantity of solution A is 25 litres less than the resultant quantity of solution B, what was the initial quantity of mixture in the tank (in litres)?
questions.solution: Let remaining mixture components A, B, and C be 7k, 8k, and 5k (Total = 20k). Final quantity of A = 7k + 15 L and Final quantity of B = 8k. Given, Final B − Final A = 25 ⇒ 8k − (7k + 15) = 25 ⇒ k = 40. Total remaining mixture = 20 × 40 = 800 L. Initial mixture = 800 L + 40 L (drained) = 840 L.

questions.question: Three friends, X, Y, and Z, are cycling on a circular track with a circumference of 2 km. They all start from the same point at 9:00 a.m. and travel in the same direction with speeds of 10 km/h, 12 km/h, and 15 km/h respectively. How many times will all three of them meet at the starting point if they continue cycling until 1:00 p.m.?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Time taken for one round = Distance ÷ Speed.
Tx = 2/10 = 1/5 h, Ty = 2/12 = 1/6 h, Tz = 2/15 h.
Time to meet at start = LCM(1/5, 1/6, 2/15) = 2/1 = 2 hours.
Total time from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. = 4 hours.
Number of meetings = Total time ÷ Meeting interval = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 times.
∴ The correct answer is 2 times.

Alternate Method
Given:
Circumference of the track (D) = 2 km
Speeds: X = 10 km/h, Y = 12 km/h, Z = 15 km/h
Cycling duration = 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. = 4 hours

Formula Used:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
Meeting time at start point = LCM of individual times taken for one round
LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators

Calculations:
⇒ Tx = 2 ÷ 10 = 1/5 h
⇒ Ty = 2 ÷ 12 = 1/6 h
⇒ Tz = 2 ÷ 15 = 2/15 h
⇒ Meeting time = LCM(1/5, 1/6, 2/15)
⇒ LCM of numerators (1, 1, 2) = 2
⇒ HCF of denominators (5, 6, 15) = 1
⇒ LCM(1/5, 1/6, 2/15) = 2 ÷ 1 = 2 hours
⇒ They all meet at the starting point every 2 hours.
⇒ Total duration from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. = 4 hours.
⇒ Number of meetings = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 times
∴ The correct answer is 2 times.

questions.question: A book publisher offers a novel to a bookstore at a 30% discount on the cover price. However, they charge an additional 5% on the discounted price for shipping. The bookstore sells the novel for ₹1620 more, earning a profit of 40%. What was the original cover price of the novel?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Let the Cover Price be 100 units.
Discounted Price = 100 − 30% = 70 units.
Total Cost Price = 70 + (5% of 70) = 73.5 units.
Profit = 40% of Cost Price = 0.40 × 73.5 = 29.4 units.

Since 29.4 units = ₹1620, Cover Price (100 units) = (1620 ÷ 29.4) × 100 ≈ ₹5510.20

∴ The correct answer is ₹5,510.20.

questions.question: A circular disc of radius 7 cm is inscribed inside an equilateral triangle. What is the approximate area of the remaining portion of the triangle?
questions.solution:
Solution

Shortcut Trick
For an equilateral triangle circumscribing a circle of radius r, the remaining area can be directly calculated as:

⇒ Remaining Area = r² × (3√3 − π)
⇒ Remaining Area = 7² × (3 × 1.732 − 3.142)
⇒ Remaining Area ≈ 49 × (5.196 − 3.142) = 49 × 2.054
⇒ Remaining Area ≈ 100.64 cm²
∴ The correct answer is 100.6 cm².

questions.question: A right triangle has sides 3, 4, and 5. A smaller triangle is drawn inside it with its vertices on the sides of the larger triangle, such that it is similar to the larger triangle. If its perimeter is 6, what is its area?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Perimeter of larger triangle = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12.
Area of larger triangle = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6.

For similar triangles, the ratio of their areas equals the square of the ratio of their perimeters.

Area of smaller triangle = 6 × (6 ÷ 12)²
⇒ Area = 6 × (1/2)² = 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5.
∴ The correct answer is 1.5 sq. units.

Alternate Method
Given:
⇒ Sides of the larger right-angled triangle = 3, 4, and 5
⇒ Perimeter of the inscribed smaller similar triangle = 6

Formula Used:
⇒ Area of a right triangle = 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular Height
⇒ For two similar triangles: Area1 / Area2 = (Perimeter1 / Perimeter2)²

Calculations:
⇒ The perimeter of the larger triangle = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12
⇒ Area of the larger triangle = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 sq. units
⇒ The ratio of their perimeters (Smaller : Larger) = 6 / 12 = 1/2
⇒ According to the similarity theorem, the ratio of their areas is the square of the scale factor.
⇒ Area Ratio = (1 / 2)² = 1 / 4
⇒ Let the area of the smaller triangle be A.
⇒ A / 6 = 1 / 4
⇒ A = 6 × (1 / 4) = 1.5 sq. units
∴ The correct answer is 1.5 sq. units.

questions.question: The distance between the centers of two circles is d. The lengths of their direct and transverse common tangents are L and M, respectively. If L² + M² = 200 and the sum of the squares of their radii is 100, what is the value of d?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
The standard identity relating the direct common tangent (L), transverse common tangent (M), distance between centers (d) and radii (r1, r2) is:

L² + M² = 2d² − 2(r1² + r2²)
Given: L² + M² = 200, and r1² + r2² = 100
⇒ 200 = 2d² − 2(100)
⇒ 2d² = 400 ⇒ d² = 200 ⇒ d = 10√2
∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance between centers = d
Direct common tangent = L
Transverse common tangent = M
Sum of squares of common tangents, L² + M² = 200
Sum of squares of radii, r1² + r2² = 100

Formula:

Length of direct common tangent (L) = √[d² − (r1 − r2)²]
Length of transverse common tangent (M) = √[d² − (r1 + r2)²]

Calculations:
Squaring both formulas to eliminate the square roots:

⇒ L² = d² − (r1² + r2² − 2r1r2)
⇒ M² = d² − (r1² + r2² + 2r1r2)

Adding both equations together:

⇒ L² + M² = d² − r1² − r2² + 2r1r2 + d² − r1² − r2² − 2r1r2
⇒ L² + M² = 2d² − 2(r1² + r2²)

Substitute the given values into the derived equation:

⇒ 200 = 2d² − 2(100)
⇒ 200 = 2d² − 200
⇒ 2d² = 400
⇒ d² = 200
⇒ d = √200 = 10√2
∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.

questions.question: There are 5 consecutive even numbers X₁, X₂, X₃, X₄, X₅ and 4 consecutive odd numbers Y₁, Y₂, Y₃, Y₄. The average of the even numbers is 4 more than the average of the odd numbers. If the sum of the even numbers is 32 more than the sum of the odd numbers, find the average of the odd numbers.
questions.solution:
Let the average of the 4 consecutive odd numbers be A.
Average of the 5 consecutive even numbers = A + 4
Given: Sum of even numbers − Sum of odd numbers = 32
⇒ 5 × (A + 4) − 4 × A = 32
⇒ 5A + 20 − 4A = 32
⇒ A = 32 - 20 = 12
∴ The correct answer is 12.

questions.question:
Aman needed ₹30,000 for a start-up and split the sum between two private lenders under simple-interest terms:
Lender A charges 9% p.a. (simple interest)
Lender B charges 6% p.a. (simple interest)
Aman kept both loans exactly 4 years and then made a single lump-sum payment that settled only the accumulated interest, which came to ₹9,600. After preparing his books of account, Aman discovered that if he interchanged the principal amounts taken from the two lenders, his four-year interest outgo would have been ₹1,200 less than what he actually paid. How much of the original ₹30,000 did Aman borrow at 9% p.a. from Lender A?
questions.solution:
Actual SI = 9600 - 1200 = ₹8400
Total interest paid in 1 year = 8400 ÷ 4 = ₹2100.
Overall average rate of interest = (2100 ÷ 30000) × 100 = 7%.
Using the Alligation method, the ratio of principals at 9% and 6% = (7 − 6) : (9 − 7) = 1 : 2.
Amount borrowed from Lender A (at 9%) = 30000 × [1 ÷ (2 + 1)] = ₹10,000.
∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.

questions.question: Sarah invested amounts in three different schemes M, N, and O at simple interest rates of 10% p.a., 12% p.a., and 15% p.a. respectively. If the total interest accrued in one year was ₹2282 and the amount invested in Scheme O was 180% of the amount invested in Scheme M and 250% of the amount invested in Scheme N, what was the amount invested in Scheme N?
questions.solution:
From the given condition, O = 1.8M and O = 2.5N.
Investment ratio M : N : O = (1 ÷ 1.8) : (1 ÷ 2.5) : 1 = 25 : 18 : 45.
Let the investments be 25 units, 18 units, and 45 units.
Total Simple Interest = (25 × 10%) + (18 × 12%) + (45 × 15%) = 2.5 + 2.16 + 6.75 = 11.41 units.
Since 11.41 units = ₹2282, 1 unit = 2282 ÷ 11.41 = ₹200.
Amount in Scheme N = 18 units = 18 × 200 = ₹3600.
∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.

questions.question: A vertical pole of height H stands on the ground. From a point P on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the pole is 60°. From a different point Q, located 10 meters away from point P (directly along the line extending from the base of the pole), the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 30°. What is the height of the pole?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
When the angle of elevation changes from \beta to \alpha over a distance d, the height H is found using: d = H \times (\cot \beta - \cot \alpha).

Here d = 10 m, \alpha = 60° and \beta = 30°:
10 = H \times (\cot 30° - \cot 60°)
10 = H \times (\sqrt{3} - 1/\sqrt{3}) \Rightarrow 10 = H \times (2/\sqrt{3})
H = 5\sqrt{3} m.

\therefore The correct answer is 5\sqrt{3} m.

Alternate Method
Given:
Distance between the two points, PQ = 10 m.
Angle of elevation from point P, \angle APB = 60°.
Angle of elevation from point Q, \angle AQB = 30°.

Formula Used:
\tan(\theta) = \text{Perpendicular} \div \text{Base}

Calculations:
Let the height of the pole AB be H and the distance PB be x.

In right-angled triangle APB:
\Rightarrow \tan(60°) = AB \div PB
\Rightarrow \sqrt{3} = H \div x
\Rightarrow x = H \div \sqrt{3}

In right-angled triangle AQB:
\Rightarrow \tan(30°) = AB \div QB
\Rightarrow 1 \div \sqrt{3} = H \div (PQ + PB)
\Rightarrow 1 \div \sqrt{3} = H \div (10 + x)
\Rightarrow 10 + x = H\sqrt{3}

Substitute the value of x:
\Rightarrow 10 + (H \div \sqrt{3}) = H\sqrt{3}
\Rightarrow 10 = H\sqrt{3} - (H \div \sqrt{3})
\Rightarrow 10 = (3H - H) \div \sqrt{3}
\Rightarrow 10 = 2H \div \sqrt{3}
\Rightarrow 2H = 10\sqrt{3}
\Rightarrow H = 5\sqrt{3} m

\therefore The correct answer is 5\sqrt{3} m.

questions.question: A right circular cone has radius of 7 cm and a height of 24 cm. A sphere is placed inside the cone such that it touches the base and the slanted surface of the cone. Find the radius of this inscribed sphere.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
The radius (r) of a sphere inscribed in a right circular cone of base radius R, height H, and slant height L is given directly by the formula:
\Rightarrow r = (R \times H) \div (R + L)
\Rightarrow L = \sqrt{R^2 + H^2} = \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{625} = 25 cm
\Rightarrow r = (7 \times 24) \div (7 + 25) = 168 \div 32
\Rightarrow r = 5.25 cm

\therefore The correct answer is 5.25 cm.

questions.question: A distributor purchases electric heaters at a price 60% above the factory's basic cost C. He gives a 25% trade discount to a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper then adds a 30% markup to his purchase price and offers customers a 10% discount on the marked price. If a customer pays ₹21,060 for one heater, what was its basic cost at the factory?
questions.solution:
Factory's basic cost = C

Distributor's price:
= 160% of C
= 1.6C

After 25% trade discount:
= 1.6C * 75/100
= 1.2C

After 30% markup by the shopkeeper:
= 1.2C * 130/100
= 1.56C

After 10% customer discount:
Final price = 1.56C * 90/100
= 1.404C

Given,
1.404C = 21,060
C = 21,060 ÷ 1.404
= ₹15,000
Therefore, the factory's basic cost was ₹15,000.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a triangle XYZ. It touches sides XY, YZ, and ZX at points A, C, and B respectively. If XB = 4.2 cm, YZ = 8 cm, and YC = 3.2 cm, then the perimeter of the triangle XYZ is:
questions.solution: We know that tangents drawn from the same point are equal. So, XB = XA = 4.2 cm. YZ = 8 cm, YC = 3.2 cm. So, CZ = YZ - YC = 8 - 3.2 = 4.8 cm and so, BZ = 4.8 cm. YC = YA = 3.2 cm. Perimeter of Triangle XYZ = XY + YZ + ZAX = (4.2 + 3.2) + 8 + (4.8 + 4.2) = 24.4 cm.

questions.question: A, B, and C can do a piece of work in 16, 24, and 32 days respectively. They start together, but C leaves after 4 days and A leaves 6 days before the completion of the work. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
Given:
A, B, and C can complete the work in 16, 24, and 32 days respectively.

They start together, but C leaves after 4 days and A leaves 6 days before the completion of the work.

Concept used:

Total work = work done each day × total time taken (in days)

Calculation:
LCM (16, 24, 32) = 96
Let the total work be LCM for the time taken by them.
Thus, total work = 96 units

efficiency,

A makes a day = 96 ÷ 16 = 6 units
B makes a day = 96 ÷ 24 = 4 units
C does a day = 96 ÷ 32 = 3 units

The entire work is completed in P days.

According to the question,

6 × (P - 6) + 4 × P + 3 × 4 = 96
⇒ 10P = 96 + 36 - 12
⇒ P = 12
∴ The work will be completed in 12 days.

questions.question: A trader earns a profit of 30% by selling an article X and loses 16% by selling another article Y. If the ratio of the cost prices of X and Y is 3 : 4, then what is the gain/loss in the entire transaction (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Given:
A trader earns a profit of 30% by selling an article X and loses 16% by selling another article Y.
The ratio of the cost prices of X and Y is 3 : 4.

Concept used:
Profit% = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100%
Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%
Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:
Let the cost price of X and Y be Rs. 300 and Rs. 400.
Total cost price = 300 + 400 = Rs. 700
Selling price of X = 300 + 300 × 30% = Rs. 390
Selling price of Y = 400 - 400 × 16% = Rs. 336
Total selling price = 390 + 336 = Rs. 726
Gain made = 726 - 700 = Rs. 26
Now, gain% in the entire transaction = (26 / 700) × 100% ≈ 3.7%
∴ The gain in the entire transaction is 3.7%.

questions.question: Ram, Shyam and Ghanshyam have ₹32, ₹46 and ₹50, respectively, with them. Their mother asks them to give her equal amounts so that the money held by them now are in continued proportion. Find the amount taken from each of them.
questions.solution:
Given:
Ram has ₹32.
Shyam has ₹46.
Ghanshyam has ₹50.
They give equal amounts to their mother such that the remaining amounts are in continued proportion.

Formula Used:
For continued proportion: a/b = b/c or b^2 = a ⋅ c.

Calculation:
Let the amount given by each of them to their mother be x.
Then, the remaining amounts are:
Ram: ₹(32 - x)
Shyam: ₹(46 - x)
Ghanshyam: ₹(50 - x)

For continued proportion:
(32 - x)/(46 - x) = (46 - x)/(50 - x)

By cross-multiplication:
(46 - x)^2 = (32 - x) ⋅ (50 - x)

Expanding both sides:
⇒ (46 - x)^2 = 32 × 50 - 32x - 50x + x^2
⇒ 2116 - 92x + x^2 = 1600 - 82x + x^2

Cancel out x^2 from both sides:
⇒ 2116 - 92x = 1600 - 82x

Simplify:
⇒ 2116 - 1600 = 92x - 82x
⇒ 516 = 10x
⇒ x = 51.6

The amount taken from each of them is ₹51.60.

questions.question: A student got 20% marks and failed by 72 marks. If he scores 40% marks then he gets 8 marks more than the passing marks. Find the passing marks.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Difference in percentage = 40% − 20% = 20%
Difference in marks = 72 (shortfall) + 8 (excess) = 80 marks
Since 20% of maximum marks = 80 marks
Passing marks = 20% marks + 72 marks = 80 + 72 = 152
∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.

Alternate Method
Given:
Marks scored in case 1 = 20% (Failed by 72 marks)
Marks scored in case 2 = 40% (8 marks more than passing marks)

Calculation:
Let the total maximum marks be x.
⇒ Passing marks = 20% of x + 72
⇒ Passing marks = 40% of x − 8

Equating both the expressions:

⇒ 20% of x + 72 = 40% of x − 8
⇒ 40% of x − 20% of x = 72 + 8
⇒ 20% of x = 80
⇒ x = (80 × 100) ÷ 20
⇒ x = 400
⇒ Passing marks = 20% of 400 + 72
⇒ Passing marks = 80 + 72 = 152
∴ The correct answer is 152 marks.

Additional Information
Passing Marks Concept
When a student fails by a certain margin, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks + Shortfall Marks.

Excess Marks Concept

When a student scores above passing marks, Passing Marks = Obtained Marks − Excess Marks.
Difference Rule

The percentage difference between the two scenarios will always be equal to the sum of the shortfall marks and the excess marks.

questions.question: If the average of a number, 50% of that number, and 25% of the same number is 280, then find the number.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick
Let the required number be 100%.

The three parts given are 100%, 50%, and 25%.

Sum of these parts = 100% + 50% + 25% = 175%
Average = 175% ÷ 3 = 280
⇒ 100% = (280 × 3 × 100) ÷ 175 = 480
∴ The correct answer is 480.

questions.question: In a circular race of 5 km on a track of circumference 1 km, two athletes run in the same direction at speeds of 20 m/s and 12 m/s. How many times will the faster athlete cross the slower athlete by the time the faster athlete finishes the race?
questions.solution:
Relative speed = 20 − 12 = 8 m/s

For one overtake, the faster athlete must gain one complete lap = 1000 m.

Time for one overtake = 1000 / 8 = 125 seconds
Time taken by the faster athlete to finish 5 km = 5000 / 20 = 250 seconds
Number of overtakes = 250 / 125 = 2
Hence, (B) is correct.

questions.question: In ∆ABC and ∆PQR, ∠ABC = ∠PRQ and ∠ACB = ∠QPR. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 15 cm and PR = 12 cm, then the measure of side QR is:
questions.solution:
Since two of the angles are similar, the triangles ABC and QRP are similar.
Therefore,
AB/BC = QR/PR
12/15 = QR/12
QR = 144/15 = 9.6 cm

questions.question: Find the value of cos²87° + cos²84° + cos²81° + ...... + cos²6° + cos²3°.
questions.solution:
cos87° = cos(90° - 3°) = sin3°
cos84° = cos(90° - 6°) = sin6°
Therefore, cos²87° + cos²84° + cos²81° + ...... + cos²6° + cos²3°
= (cos²87° + cos²3°) + (cos²84° + cos²6°)... to 14 terms + cos²45°
= (sin²3° + cos²3°) + (sin²6° + cos²6°)... to 14 terms + 1/2
= 14 + 1/2 = 29/2

questions.question: If the equation of a line is y = 3x - 5, what is the slope of the line?
questions.solution:
Formula:
Equation of a line in slope-intercept form is:
y = mx + c
Where:
m = slope of the line
c = y-intercept
Given equation:
y = 3x - 5
Comparing with:
y = mx + c
m = 3
Therefore, the slope of the line is 3.
